```{=html}
<div class="project-intro">

  <div class="project-image">
    <img src="../images/Flexible_photo.png" alt="Flexible Measuring Laser">
    <div class="project-caption">The Flexible Measuring Laser system.</div>
  </div>

  <div class="project-text">
    <h2>Background</h2>

    <p>Users of the Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) are required to manually estimate the height of their mounted samples before placing them inside the microscope chamber. This estimation — typically done by visually comparing the sample against a ruler — is inherently inconsistent and prone to error. Inaccurate height inputs can lead to collisions inside the chamber, causing damage to sensitive detectors or degrading microscope performance.</p>

    <p>The client requested a height measurement solution that would allow trained users to quickly, safely, and accurately determine the maximum sample height for any standard SEM sample holder. The solution needed to accommodate all existing holder bases with at most a 10 cm radius, provide readout tolerances within 0.5 mm, and critically — make no contact with the top surface of the sample, which is coated in a conductive layer only nanometers thick that could be irreparably damaged by even the lightest touch.</p>
  </div>

</div>

<p>To meet these requirements, I designed a precision rack and pinion Z-axis measurement system integrated with a laser and photosensor, paired with a slew bearing for radial motion. This allowed the system to sweep around the sample and detect its tallest point without ever making contact. The entire measurement process was designed to be completed in under two minutes by a trained non-specialist user.</p>

<p>Material selection was a critical part of the design process. Through a full fatigue and material analysis, I selected PLA for its scalability and ease of use in 3D printing — ensuring the device would remain accurate, durable, and easily replicable over its lifetime. The final design prevents $1000+ in potential equipment damage from improper sample height inputs.</p>
```
